novel_features.name: One-command food logging
novel_features.description: Search foods by Czech text and log one to the diary in a single command, with the right meal slot.
novel_features.rationale: Only possible because the local FTS5 store caches autocomplete results; the upstream web requires five clicks per food.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Choose this when an agent or user wants to log a known food without first looking up its id.

novel_features.name: Macro target gap across window
novel_features.description: Across the last N days, show how much of each macro target remains, optionally grouped by meal slot.
novel_features.rationale: Requires cached daily summaries joined with diary entries — no single endpoint produces this windowed view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs to reason about meal planning that hits weekly targets, not single-day totals.

novel_features.name: Energy-in vs energy-out balance
novel_features.description: Joins per-day diary energy with activity energy from the local store; prints daily series and 7/14-day moving average.
novel_features.rationale: Combines diary + activity tables in SQLite; the web UI never joins them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for athletes whose fuelling depends on day-to-day training load.

novel_features.name: Diary frequency analysis
novel_features.description: Counts how often each foodstuff appears in your diary over a window. Surfaces dietary monotony or staple frequencies.
novel_features.rationale: Pure SQLite GROUP BY over cached diary entries; web UI shows one day at a time.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when you need 'what does this user actually eat?' rather than 'what's documented for one day'.

novel_features.name: Macro-similar food substitutes
novel_features.description: Given a foodstuff, find others in the local store with similar macro profile per 100 g; rank by Euclidean distance.
novel_features.rationale: Only works because JSON-LD on every food detail page is parsed into typed nutrition; web UI has no similar-foods view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to swap a food for one that hits a different macro target without changing the calorie ballpark.

novel_features.name: Allergen mining from JSON-LD
novel_features.description: Extracts Czech allergen tokens (lepek, laktóza, vejce, ořechy, sója, ryby) from the JSON-LD keywords on a food detail page.
novel_features.rationale: Allergens are not in any API field — they're scattered through the JSON-LD `keywords` array and the prose description; nobody else extracts them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when filtering foods for a user with dietary restrictions, before the web UI would ever surface that data.

novel_features.name: Plan a meal to hit a protein target
novel_features.description: Given remaining macro budget for the day, greedy-selects from favorites + most-frequent foods that close the protein gap within an energy ceiling.
novel_features.rationale: Joins today's summary + favorites + frequency analysis; no single API call does this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs to suggest 'what should this person eat next' grounded in foods they actually like.

novel_features.name: Weight linear regression with projection
novel_features.description: OLS regression on weight history; reports slope (kg/week), R^2, and days-to-target at current trajectory.
novel_features.rationale: Math over `monthWeight[]` from the summary endpoint; web UI shows a chart but no slope or projection.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for coaching conversations grounded in 'you're losing 0.4 kg/week' rather than chart-eyeball.

novel_features.name: Bulk diary export to JSON
novel_features.description: Pulls N days of diary into one JSON document with typed nutrition totals per day. Agent-friendly bulk format.
novel_features.rationale: Iterates cached daily diary; the web UI only exports per-day PDF/XLS.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs to load a coaching client's diary into a pandas DataFrame or pipe it through analytics.

novel_features.name: Undo last diary entry
novel_features.description: Removes the most recently added diary entry from the cached last-logged record.
novel_features.rationale: Cached last-added entry id makes the delete endpoint addressable; the web UI requires finding the row visually.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to recover from a misclicked log without hunting through the day's meal slots.

narrative.headline: Every Kalorické Tabulky feature plus offline FTS5 search, macro-gap windowing, and weight regression — agent-ready Czech nutrition tracking.
narrative.value_prop: Czech-language nutrition CLI for kaloricketabulky.cz. Search 244 000 foods with diacritics-tolerant FTS5, log meals in one command via local food cache, compute macro gaps across weeks, regress weight, mine allergens — every endpoint the web app uses, plus 10 transcendence features the web app refuses to expose.
narrative.auth_narrative: Authenticate with `auth login --email <you>` (password read from stdin, MD5-hashed before sending, then discarded). The cookie session is stored at `~/.config/kaloricke-tabulky/session`. To avoid a password on disk, use `auth login --chrome` to import the session cookies directly from a logged-in Chrome profile. Run `auth refresh` to extend the session.

quickstart.comment: Authenticate once; password is MD5-hashed locally before sending and never written to disk.
Czech-language food search; results come from the live autocomplete API or local FTS5 cache.
Resolve the food by name and log it in one command.
Daily summary trimmed to the fields you care about.
Where this week's macros fell short, by meal slot.

troubleshoots.symptom: auth login returns code 0 but later calls 401
troubleshoots.fix: Check that you're not behind a corporate proxy that strips Set-Cookie. Try `auth login --chrome` instead.

troubleshoots.symptom: Czech food search returns no results
troubleshoots.fix: Search uses diacritics-folded match; if your input has unusual punctuation, try plain ASCII (e.g. 'tvaroh' instead of 'Tvaroh měkký').

troubleshoots.symptom: diary log says food not found
troubleshoots.fix: Run `food search <text>` first to verify a match; if FTS5 cache is stale, run `sync foodstuffs` to repopulate.

troubleshoots.symptom: weight regression complains 'not enough data points'
troubleshoots.fix: Regression needs at least 3 weight entries within the window. Lower `--days` or log more weights.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when you need automated or agentic access to Kalorické Tabulky data — bulk diary exports, multi-day macro analytics, weight trend regression, allergen filtering, or quick food logging. It is Czech-language-aware (diacritics-folded search) and handles the kJ/kcal duality natively. Not the right tool for ad-hoc browser-only sessions where the web UI is faster.
